question: Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose formed the Indian Association in the year _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1876**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Surendranath Banerjee laid the foundations of the Indian National Movement by founding the Indian Association at Calcutta in 1876.
 
• On July 26, 1876, Banerjee along with Ananda Mohan Bose formed the ‘Indian Association’ in Kolkata.
 
• This Association aimed to unify Indian people on a common political program.
 
• The Association merged with the Indian National Congress in 1885.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was a skilled orator. 
 
• He organized a huge public meeting against this decision on 24 March 1877, in Town Hall, Kolkata.
 
• He was the second Indian to qualify for the Indian Civil Service examinations.
 
• He resolved to bring the whole of India on a common platform, on civil services in particular, but also all policies affecting Indians in general.
 
• He wanted an India unified in the matter of political aspiration and program.
 
• He was also a part of the nine-member Congress delegation to England in 1890.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Organizations 
 Year
 Features
 
 

 The Poon Sarvajanik Sabha 
 1870 
 
 
 
• It was led by Mahadev Govind Ranade.
 
• They organized a successful campaign among the peasants, as well as at Poona and Bombay against the land revenue settlement of 1867.
 
• This agitation generated a mentality of resistance among the peasants which contributed to the rise of peasant protest in 1875.
 
• The Sabha, as well as many of the nationalist newspapers, also supported the Deccan Agriculturists‘, Relief Bill.
 
• Under its impact, a large number of peasants refused to pay the enhanced revenue.
 
 
 
 

 The Indian Association
 1876
 
 
 
• The Indian National Association also known as the Indian Association was the first avowed nationalist organization founded in British India by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose.
 
• The objectives of this Association were "promoting by every legitimate means the political, intellectual and material advancement of the people".
 
• This association opposed Elbert's bill on the dispute as lowering the age limit for civil service examination.
 
 
 
 

 Madras Mahajana Sabha
 1884
 
 
 
• It was established by M. Veeraraghavachariar, S. Ramaswami Mudaliar, and P. Anandacharlu. 
 
• The Madras Mahajan Sabha was formed in May 1884 to coordinate the activities of the local association and to ‘provide a focus for the non-official intelligence spread up through the Presidency’.
 
 
 
 

 The Bombay Presidency Association
 1885
 
 
 
• The Bombay Presidency Association was started by Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozshah Mehta, and K.T. Telang in 1885.
